subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Expected behavior derived first: under standard-binary, operand-1 ** 0 with operand-1 nonzero yields exactly the SBIDI value 1 (§8.8.1.4.4 rule 1). READ: NumericRenderer.Power (NumericRenderer.cs:544-553) is the ONE exponentiation dispatch. Its standard arm is `if (StandardDecimal) return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DecPow(DecOperand(b), DecOperand(e), IntermediateMode), 0, Dec: true);` and `internal bool StandardDecimal => ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or ArithmeticMode.Standard` (NumericRenderer.cs:559). ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary is NOT in that set -- the two-arm dispatch has a standard-decimal arm and a native default, and no standard-binary arm; a StandardBinary compile would fall through to the native Int128/binary64 path (CombineNative / PowNativeInt), which is a DIFFERENT algorithm from the SBIDI one this rule mandates. That fall-through is unreachable today only because DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) fails the compile with COBOL0806 first -- and I verified the unreachability by reading, not assuming: EditionContext.Error (EditionContext.cs:109) is unconditional (`error {code}:`), has no --permissive branch, and OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf (OptionsBinder.cs:68) is the sole producer of the enum value. The §8.8.1.5.4 twin of this rule IS implemented (CobolDec.Pow, reached through RuntimeApi.DecPow) -- that is the structural template a standard-binary implementation would mirror, and its existence is why this row is NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than merely unwritten. Editions 2014,2023 (F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an SBIDI Pow with rule 1's x**0 => 1 leg plus a golden under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY. No qualifying test. || UPHELD, with the line references corrected: I opened NumericRenderer.cs and read the dispatch myself. `private NumX Power(NumX b, NumX e, bool expIsNonNegativeLiteral = false)` is at line 543 (not 544), its standard arm `if (StandardDecimal) return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DecPow(DecOperand(b), DecOperand(e), IntermediateMode), 0, Dec: true);` at :551-552, and the predicate `internal bool StandardDecimal => ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or ArithmeticMode.Standard;` is at line 394, NOT :559 -- the adjudicator's :559 points into the middle of Power's comment block. The SUBSTANCE is exactly right: I enumerated every read of the mode in the whole tree (`grep -rn 'Options.Arithmetic' src/`) and got six sites -- ExpressionBinder.cs:666 and NumericRenderer.cs:394 test {StandardDecimal, Standard}; IntrinsicBinder.cs:2349/:2376/:2429 test StandardDecimal alone; IntrinsicBinder.cs:2356 is the only StandardBinary arm in the compiler and it is a §15.83.3-r3 usage BAN, not an arithmetic implementation; StatementValidation.cs:107 tests != Native. Nothing renders a standard-binary exponentiation, so rule 1's x**0 => 1 has no SBIDI implementation and the mode falls to the native default arm. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
